chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Bahri, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt due from another man, and the debtor sells wine and pigs in his presence to collect the payment. He said, 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to collect a debt by selling wine or pigs in the debtor's presence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the validity of debt settlement does not depend on the purity or commonality of the goods used, provided the creditor accepts them willingly. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of *istihsan* (equity) in commercial transactions, distinguishing between the intrinsic impurity of the item and its utility as a medium of exchange for discharging financial obligations.
